framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Ethics > Fairness, bias and discrimination > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Apply bias mitigation and fairness evaluation across the entire AI project life cycle; comply with human rights law, the Equality Act 2010, the Public Sector Equality Duty and EHRC guidance; review outputs and decisions for bias by measuring results for different groups, including intersectional groups; set up feedback routes for unfair decisions or harmful outputs; evaluate continuously as fairness expectations change.
what_is_tested: Bias and fairness of outputs across groups, incl. intersectional
interpretation_note: Practical recommendations in a non-statutory playbook; PSED and Equality Act duties themselves are binding law, but the testing steps are recommendations.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Practical recommendations > Applies to generative AI
requirement_paraphrase: Treat LLM-generated code as inherently insecure and never use it in production without a code review; train users not to trust or rely solely on generative AI outputs; filter malicious URLs if links are included in LLM responses.
what_is_tested: Security review of LLM-generated code before production
interpretation_note: Release gate for AI-generated code rather than testing of the AI system itself.

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Security > Security risks > Using AI > Data and model poisoning
requirement_paraphrase: To counter data and model poisoning, model outputs should be tested against known good responses and systematically tested for bias.
what_is_tested: Output integrity against known-good responses; bias
interpretation_note: Mitigation text attached to a named security risk.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3.3 'When deploying, continuously monitor and test', case study 'GovTech: Phased rollouts of coding assistants', pp.42-43
requirement_paraphrase: Case study: GovTech (statutory board) rolled out agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, GitHub Copilot Agent Mode from Oct 2025; Claude Code from Apr 2026) after extensive tests on failure and threat vectors such as agent manipulation, hallucination and MCP server compromise and after implementing controls; phase 1 limited to GovTech employees, no MCP access and low-risk systems; before phase 2 (other agencies, then vendors) red teaming was conducted to validate guardrails, with central logging and a sandboxed MCP governance path.
what_is_tested: Agentic coding assistants: manipulation, hallucination, MCP compromise; guardrail effectiveness
interpretation_note: Descriptive public-sector practice inside a voluntary framework; shows a staged pre-deployment test and phased rollout by a government agency, not a requirement.

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (v1.5, published 2026-05-20, updated 2026-06-05)
clause_or_page: s.2.3 overview p.33 and s.2.3.3 'Robust change management', p.45
requirement_paraphrase: Throughout the lifecycle implement change management and version control; define triggers that start a change review (technical e.g. model updates or tool changes; environmental; performance e.g. anomalous behaviour; regulatory) and categorise changes by risk, with lighter review for minor prompt refinements, full governance review for material changes such as model updates or autonomy adjustments, and possibly an immediate re-risk assessment for critical changes affecting high-stakes decisions.
what_is_tested: Change-triggered review and re-assessment of agentic systems
interpretation_note: New in v1.5 ('What's new', p.5). Complements Singapore-034 (gradual rollout, monitoring).
